subject: Pilot: No-training and ownership assurances — next steps
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudmed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: No-train commitment & prompt/response ownership for POC

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudMed is excited to move the pilot forward with Redwood. Before we sign the statement of work, procurement and legal have a few specific asks around data handling and rights that we need clarified in the DPA:

- No-training / no-model-improvement: our customers require that data sent to the service for the pilot not be used to improve any model weights or prompt-tuning artifacts.
- Prompt/response ownership: CloudMed needs confirmation that prompts and responses we submit remain our data and that we retain exclusive rights to export them.
- Subprocessor list & residency: a current subprocessor registry and confirmation of any cross-border transfers for logs or telemetry.
- Evidence for ops: we may need a short ops/evidence pack (logs, KMS residency, export options) to satisfy procurement.

Attached is a PDF with the procurement checklist and our preferred DPA questions (CloudMed_DPA_questions.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the no-train assurance for the pilot, and what operational evidence you can deliver? We'd prefer to finalize terms this week and schedule a 30-minute call with your legal/ops.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement
CloudMed Health

(Attachment: CloudMed_DPA_questions.pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudmed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: No-training commitment & prompt/response ownership for POC

Hi Elena — copying in Jordan and Marissa, thanks for outlining CloudMed's requirements.

We can commit to the following for the pilot period (and document this in a DPA addendum):

- No-training (pilot scope): Redwood will not use, include, or incorporate CloudMed customer data into model training, fine-tuning, or other model-improvement activities. This includes offline retraining pipelines and any prompt-tuning collections.
- Telemetry carveouts: platform telemetry required for availability/latency monitoring will be collected in aggregated form only and will not contain customer prompt/response content. We will provide a sample telemetry schema.
- Prompt/response custody: CloudMed retains ownership of prompts and responses. Redwood will provide export tooling (SFTP + API export) and a documented retention policy for any ephemeral logs used for debugging.
- Subprocessors & residency: we maintain a live subprocessor registry; we'll provide a snapshot for the pilot. Any persistent logs destined for long-term storage will be routed per the agreed residency (we can agree to US-only residency for this pilot).

Operational evidence we can assemble for procurement:
- Subprocessor registry snapshot (signed statement)
- KMS residency attestation and key management summary
- Export flow diagram + SFTP delivery test plan
- No-train ops checklist with controls we use to prevent data leakage into training (attached: no-train-ops-checklist.xlsx)

A couple of caveats and proposed language: for service integrity we reserve the right to process content for abuse detection and policy enforcement; those signals are strictly isolated and not used for model updates. If CloudMed needs cryptographic proof of non-training (e.g., snapshot logs signed by a third party), we can discuss an escrow or audit window.

If that aligns, Jordan — please confirm one of the proposed call times and we'll kick off with the redline draft.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: no-train-ops-checklist.xlsx)
